extracted.intended_audience: authors, publishers, and ALSC/Newbery committee members (people submitting or evaluating books for the Newbery Medal)
extracted.subtask_description: Rules, definitions, and evaluation criteria for eligibility and selection of the John Newbery Medal (most distinguished American children's book published in the preceding year). Includes procedural submission requirements for entrants and guidance for committee deliberation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Award scope and core eligibility (Terms #1)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Medal shall be awarded annually to the author of the most distinguished contribution to American literature for children published by an American publisher in the United States in English during the preceding year. There are no limitations as to the character of the book considered except that it be original work. Honor books may be named. These shall be books that are also truly distinguished.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This single statement sets the primary eligibility: author, most distinguished contribution, American literature for children, published in the U.S. in English in the preceding year, and original work. It also allows naming honor books. Use this to determine the candidate pool.

rubrics_metrics.name: Author citizenship/residency restriction (Terms #2)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Award is restricted to authors who are citizens or residents of the United States.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Residency (see definition) qualifies authors who are not citizens. Verify author citizenship or residency when determining eligibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Committee must consider only eligible books (Terms #3)
rubrics_metrics.description: The committee in its deliberations is to consider only the books eligible for the award, as specified in the terms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Committee members should exclude any work that does not meet the terms/definitions (language, publication date, originality, publisher, author residency). Eligibility determinations are confided to the committee.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: 'Contribution to American literature' (Definitions #1)
rubrics_metrics.description: “Contribution to American literature” indicates the text of a book. It also implies that the committee shall consider all forms of writing—fiction, non-fiction, and poetry. Reprints, compilations and abridgements are not eligible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focus is on the text (not ancillary materials). All textual forms are within scope, but previously published/reprinted/compiled/abridged texts are excluded.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: 'Contribution ... for children' (Definitions #2)
rubrics_metrics.description: A “contribution to American literature for children” shall be a book for which children are an intended potential audience. The book displays respect for children’s understandings, abilities, and appreciations. Children are defined as persons of ages up to and including fourteen, and books for this entire age range are to be considered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When evaluating, determine whether children (≤14) are an intended audience and whether the book treats their capacities respectfully. Books aimed at different parts of that age range are all eligible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: 'Distinguished' (Definitions #3)
rubrics_metrics.description: “Distinguished” is defined as: marked by eminence and distinction; noted for significant achievement; marked by excellence in quality; marked by conspicuous excellence or eminence; individually distinct.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these descriptors as the standard for selection—seek works exhibiting eminence, significant achievement, and conspicuous excellence; 'distinguished' is the core qualitative bar.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: 'Author' (Definitions #4)
rubrics_metrics.description: “Author” may include co-authors. The author(s) may be awarded the medal posthumously.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Co-authored works are eligible and posthumous awards are permitted; treat joint authorship and posthumous circumstances as allowable under the rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: 'Original work' (Definitions #5)
rubrics_metrics.description: The term 'original work' means that the text was created by this writer and no one else. It may include original retellings of traditional literature, provided the words are the author’s own. Further, 'original work' means that the text is presented here for the first time and has not been previously published elsewhere in this or any other form. Text reprinted or compiled from other sources are not eligible. Abridgements are not eligible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Verify both authorship and first publication: retellings are acceptable only if the wording is new and by the submitting author; anything previously published in any form (reprint, compilation, abridgement) is ineligible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: 'In English' (Definitions #6)
rubrics_metrics.description: “In English” means that the committee considers only books written and published in English. This requirement DOES NOT limit the use of words or phrases in another language where appropriate in context.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Primary text must be in English, but occasional non-English words/phrases used contextually are allowed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: 'American literature published in the United States' (Definitions #7)
rubrics_metrics.description: “American literature published in the United States” means that books first published in previous years in other countries are not eligible. Books published simultaneously in the U.S. and another country may be eligible. Books published in a U.S. territory, or U.S. commonwealth are eligible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check original publication history: works first published abroad in earlier years are excluded; simultaneous multi-country publication may qualify; U.S. territories/commonwealth publications qualify as U.S. publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: 'Published…in the preceding year' (Definitions #8)
rubrics_metrics.description: “Published…in the preceding year” means that the book has a publication date in that year, was available for purchase in that year, and has a copyright date no later than that year. A book might have a copyright date prior to the year under consideration but, for various reasons, was not published until the year under consideration. If a book is published prior to its year of copyright as stated in the book, it shall be considered in its year of copyright as stated in the book. The intent of the definition is that every book be eligible for consideration, but that no book be considered in more than one year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Determine eligibility by the book's stated publication and copyright dates and actual availability; ensure each book is considered only in its appropriate year.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: 'Resident' (Definitions #9)
rubrics_metrics.description: “Resident” specifies that the author has established and maintains a residence in the United States, U.S. territory, or U.S. commonwealth as distinct from being a casual or occasional visitor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Residency implies an established, maintained presence—short-term visitors do not qualify as residents for eligibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: Committee focus on eligible year only (Definitions #10)
rubrics_metrics.description: The term, “only the books eligible for the award,” specifies that the committee is not to consider the entire body of the work by an author or whether the author has previously won the award. The committee’s decision is to be made following deliberation about the books of the specified calendar year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judgment must be based solely on the book(s) published in the eligible year; avoid influence from an author's backlist or prior awards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Literary elements to consider when identifying 'distinguished' text (Criteria 1a)
rubrics_metrics.description: Committee members need to consider the following: interpretation of the theme or concept; presentation of information including accuracy, clarity, and organization; development of a plot; delineation of characters; delineation of a setting; appropriateness of style.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are the substantive literary dimensions used to assess distinction. The note clarifies that excellence may not be expected in every listed element for every book, but the book should have distinguished qualities in all elements pertinent to its content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Excellence of presentation for a child audience (Criteria 1b)
rubrics_metrics.description: Committee members must consider excellence of presentation for a child audience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether the book's presentation (language, structure, clarity, pacing, etc.) is especially effective for children within the intended age range.

rubrics_metrics.name: Primacy of text; role of other components (Criteria 2)
rubrics_metrics.description: Each book is to be considered as a contribution to American literature. The committee is to make its decision primarily on the text. Other components of a book, such as illustrations, overall design of the book, etc., may be considered when they make the book less effective.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize textual literary quality in evaluation. Consider illustrations/design only insofar as they detract from (not enhance) the book's effectiveness as literature for children.

rubrics_metrics.name: Self-contained nature of the book (Criteria 3)
rubrics_metrics.description: The book must be a self-contained entity, not dependent on other media (i.e., sound or film equipment) for its enjoyment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ineligible are works that require external media to be understood or enjoyed; award focuses on the book as an independent literary object.

rubrics_metrics.name: Award intent: not for didactic content or popularity (Note)
rubrics_metrics.description: The award is for literary quality and quality presentation for children. The award is not for didactic content or popularity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not equate educational/didactic merit or sales/popularity with the 'distinguished' literary standard; focus evaluation on artistic and presentation excellence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission requirement: complete form and mail one copy (Submission Information)
rubrics_metrics.description: How to submit books for consideration for the Newbery Medal: Complete the award submission form. Mail one copy of the book to the award committee chair. Address information available upon completion of submission form (see first bullet above). The deadline for submitting works is December 31 of the publication year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the submission form process, send one physical copy to the committee chair by Dec 31 of the publication year; check the form for the current chair address.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission logistics and office policies (Submission Information - notes)
rubrics_metrics.description: ALSC membership is not a requirement to submit your work. If you wish, you may attach a cover letter with your contact information to your final work. There is no submission form to fill out (besides address request), nor an entry fee for the Newbery Medal. The ALSC office is only requesting for one copy to be sent to the committee chair. Neither the ALSC office nor the committee chair can confirm receipt of submissions. If you would like to confirm delivery receipt of your submission please use a tracking number for your package. Submissions that are dropped off in-person to the ALSC office will not be accepted. The ALSC office cannot answer eligibility questions or advise on which award your submission is eligible for. It is up to you to review the terms and criteria and if you feel you qualify, submit as appropriate. Eligibility is determined by the committee and is confidential.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical guidance for submitters: only one mailed copy, no entry fee, optional cover letter allowed, do not drop off in-person, use tracked shipping if you need receipt confirmation, ALSC staff will not rule on eligibility—committee does.
